docs.title: Welcome to NFRAOPS
docs.text: This is the GitHub organization website for NFRAOPS, built with MkDocs and featuring a ClickHouse-inspired dark theme.

docs.title: Quick Navigation
docs.text:
• Architecture - System architecture and design decisions
  • Diagrams - PlantUML diagrams and visual documentation

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
This site is built with MkDocs and served locally using:

make serve

For detailed setup instructions, see the repository README.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Static Documentation: Pure MkDocs static site, no server-side processing
  • ClickHouse Theme: Dark theme inspired by ClickHouse design (pure black background, neon accents)
  • Poetry-Powered: Modern Python dependency management with Poetry
  • Automated Deployment: Auto-deploys to GitHub Pages on push to main branch
  • Container Support: Docker support for consistent development environments

docs.title: About NFRAOPS
docs.text: NFRAOPS is dedicated to building and maintaining infrastructure documentation and operational excellence.

docs.title: Mission
docs.text: To provide comprehensive, accessible documentation for infrastructure operations and architecture decisions.

docs.text:

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: This section contains architecture documentation and design decisions for the NFRAOPS infrastructure.

docs.title: Sections
docs.text: • Decisions - Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The NFRAOPS infrastructure is designed with simplicity and automation in mind: - Static documentation websites for knowledge sharing - Git-native deployment workflows - Containerized development environments - Poetry-driven Python tooling

docs.title: Key Principles
docs.text:
1. Simplicity First: All systems remain simple, clear, and compact
  2. Git-Native: Deployments happen through Git workflows
  3. Automation: Common operations exposed as Makefile targets
  4. Modern Python: Uses Poetry for dependency management and Python 3.11+

docs.title: Architecture Decision Records
docs.text: This section contains Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) for the NFRAOPS infrastructure.

docs.title: What are ADRs?
docs.text: Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) document important architectural decisions along with their context and consequences.

docs.title: ADR Format
docs.text:
Each ADR follows this structure:

  • Status: Current state of the decision (proposed, accepted, deprecated, superseded)
  • Context: Problem context and background
  • Decision: The decision made
  • Consequences: Impact of the decision

docs.title: Creating ADRs
docs.text:
To create a new ADR, use:

make adr-new TITLE="Your Decision Title"

This will create a new numbered ADR file with the proper template.

docs.title: Diagrams

docs.text: See PlantUML Guide for information on creating and using diagrams in this documentation.

docs.title: Diagram Types
docs.text:
• System Context: High-level system overviews
  • Component Diagrams: Detailed component architectures
  • Sequence Diagrams: Interaction flows between components
  • Deployment Diagrams: Infrastructure and deployment patterns

docs.title: Creating Diagrams
docs.text:
Diagrams are created using PlantUML syntax in markdown files. The mkdocs-puml plugin automatically renders these during site build.

Example:

@startuml
Alice -> Bob: Hello
Bob -> Alice: Hi!
@enduml

docs.title: PlantUML Guide
docs.text: This guide explains how to create and use PlantUML diagrams in the NFRAOPS documentation.

docs.title: What is PlantUML?
docs.text:
PlantUML is a tool that allows you to create diagrams from a simple textual description. It supports various diagram types including:

  • Sequence diagrams
  • Use case diagrams
  • Class diagrams
  • Activity diagrams
  • Component diagrams
  • State diagrams
  • Deployment diagrams

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text: Diagrams are created using PlantUML syntax in markdown files. The mkdocs-puml plugin automatically renders these during site build.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
@startuml
Alice -> Bob: Hello
Bob -> Alice: Hi!
@enduml

docs.title: Sequence Diagram
docs.text:
@startuml
actor User
participant "First Class" as A
participant "Second Class" as B

User -> A : DoSomething()
A -> B : ProcessRequest()
B --> A : Response
A --> User : Result
@enduml

docs.title: Component Diagram
docs.text:
@startuml
[Component] as Comp
[Database] as DB

Comp --> DB : Reads/Writes
@enduml

docs.title: Activity Diagram
docs.text:
@startuml
start
:ReadRequest;
if (RequestValid?) then (yes)
  :ProcessRequest;
  :SendResponse;
else (no)
  :SendError;
endif
stop
@enduml

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Keep diagrams simple: Complex diagrams are hard to understand
  2. Use descriptive labels: Clear labels make diagrams self-documenting
  3. Maintain consistency: Use similar styling across related diagrams
  4. Document assumptions: Add notes for complex business logic
  5. Version control: Text-based diagrams are easy to track in git

docs.title: Rendering
docs.text:
The site uses the PlantUML server for rendering. Diagrams are cached for performance.

For local development, ensure you have internet connectivity to reach the PlantUML server.

docs.title: Admonitions
docs.text: Admonitions are callout boxes that highlight important information.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Note Title

This is a note admonition.

Tip Title

This is a tip admonition.

Warning Title

This is a warning admonition.

Danger Title

This is a danger admonition.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
• note: Informational notes
  • tip: Helpful suggestions
  • warning: Warnings and cautions
  • danger: Critical warnings

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Note

This is a standard note for general information.

Best Practice

Always use clear, descriptive titles for your admonitions.

Breaking Change

This API will change in the next release.

Security Risk

Never commit secrets or credentials to the repository.

docs.title: Code Highlighting
docs.text: This site uses PyMdown extensions for syntax highlighting.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: Code blocks are automatically highlighted based on the language specified in the fence.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
def hello_world():
    print("Hello, World!")

echo "Hello from the shell"

docs.title: Supported Languages
docs.text:
• Python
  • Bash
  • YAML
  • JavaScript
  • JSON
  • And many more...

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Syntax highlighting is configured through: - pymdownx.highlight extension - Pygments for syntax highlighting - Material theme for styling
